title: Complications and Advanced Watchmaking
description: After the simple movement is honest: calendars, chronographs, automatic winding, tourbillons, and the finishing a service actually protects.

sourceReferences.title: WOSTEP Chronograph / Chronometry
sourceReferences.notes: Chronograph as a later specialization. Timing remains a discipline. Tourbillon is not a beginner object.

sourceReferences.title: HSNY education ladder
sourceReferences.notes: Complications sit after 101–104, not inside them.

modules.title: Timekeeping extras
learningObjectives: Add calendar, GMT, winding, or reserve indication without rewriting the timebase
Trace which wheel actually drives the extra hand or disc

modules.title: Chronograph
modules.blurb: A stopwatch grafted onto a watch.
learningObjectives: Start, stop, and reset a seconds register coupled to the going train
Distinguish column-wheel, cam, flyback, and rattrapante by what they add

modules.title: High complications and finishing
modules.blurb: Tourbillon, striking, what a service is.
learningObjectives: State the positional error a tourbillon averages, and when it does not
Treat finishing, service, certificates, and silicon as mechanisms or claims, not luxury

concepts.name: Simple date
concepts.summary: A 31-tooth wheel the motion works advances once a day.
objectives: Advance a date disc once a day from the motion works
Predict a jammed setting if you force the date near the changeover

concepts.name: Annual and perpetual calendars
concepts.summary: Remembering months, and sometimes leap years.
objectives: Distinguish simple, annual, and perpetual calendars by what they remember
Predict which one needs a human in February

concepts.name: Moonphase
concepts.summary: A 59-tooth compromise with the sky.
objectives: Drive a moon disc from a reduction that approximates the lunation
State the error a 59-tooth disc accepts on purpose

concepts.name: GMT and world time
concepts.summary: A second hour hand, or a disc of cities.
objectives: Add a 24-hour hand that can be set independently of local time
Distinguish a true GMT from a world-time disc that only shows cities

concepts.name: Alarm
concepts.summary: A second barrel whose job is noise.
objectives: Store a second spring or a second release so a hammer can strike
Predict what the alarm must not do to the going train's rate

concepts.name: Automatic winding
concepts.summary: A rotor that winds so the wearer does not have to.
objectives: Convert a rotor's motion into winding without letting the spring overwind
Trace a reversing gear or a slipping bridle as the safety

concepts.name: The rotor
concepts.summary: A weight that turns, and the reverser that makes both ways count.
objectives: Name the rotor as the mass that turns with the wearer's motion
Predict unidirectional versus bidirectional winding from the reverser

concepts.name: Power-reserve indication
concepts.summary: A hand that tracks the barrel, not the time.
objectives: Indicate remaining spring without stealing the timebase
Trace the differential or cone that turns reserve into a hand

concepts.name: Chronograph
concepts.summary: Start, stop, reset — a second train clutched in.
objectives: Couple a seconds register to the going train, then uncouple it
Predict what a dragging clutch does to amplitude while the chrono runs

concepts.name: Column wheel versus cam
concepts.summary: How the pusher's logic is remembered.
objectives: Contrast a column wheel with a cam as the sequencer of start, stop, reset
Predict a sloppy pusher feel when the cam's edges are worn

concepts.name: Reset and hammers
concepts.summary: Hearts on the chronograph wheels, and the hammers that find them.
objectives: Drop hammers onto hearts so the hands return to zero
Predict a hand that does not zero if a heart or hammer is bent

concepts.name: Flyback
concepts.summary: Reset that restarts without a separate stop.
objectives: Reset and restart in one pusher action while the chrono is running
State the extra clutch work a flyback demands

concepts.name: Rattrapante
concepts.summary: A split seconds hand that can wait.
objectives: Split a seconds hand so one can freeze while the other runs
Predict the clamp that holds the split hand and then lets it catch up

concepts.name: The tourbillon
concepts.summary: Averaging positional error, and when it is theater.
objectives: State that a tourbillon averages gravitational positional error by rotating the cage
Predict an error that has the same sign in every position and will not cancel

concepts.name: When a tourbillon is theater
concepts.summary: A wrist is not a pocket. Rotation does not cancel every error.
objectives: Say when a rotating cage is theater on a wrist that already changes position
Compare a well-regulated fixed escapement with a cage that does not change the mean

concepts.name: Minute repeater
concepts.summary: Sounding the time with racks and snails.
objectives: Read hours, quarters, and minutes by hammers on gongs
Trace the snail and rack that decide how many blows to strike

concepts.name: Striking work
concepts.summary: A second gear train whose product is sound.
objectives: Distinguish a repeater you demand from a clock that strikes itself
Predict the power a striking work must not steal from the going train

concepts.name: Equation of time
concepts.summary: The difference between sundial noon and mean noon.
objectives: Display the difference between mean solar time and apparent solar time
Name the cam that approximates the equation of time

concepts.name: Finishing
concepts.summary: Decorative finishing, surface preparation, and lubrication as distinct jobs.
objectives: Treat decorative finishing, surface preparation, and lubrication as distinct jobs
Refuse to treat anglage or perlage as an oil-management mechanism without a sourced claim

concepts.name: What a service actually does
concepts.summary: Clean, oil, adjust — not a battery.
objectives: Name a service as disassembly, cleaning, oil, and a check of freedoms
Predict what 'just oil it through the caseback' leaves dirty

concepts.name: COSC and certificates
concepts.summary: A protocol, not a personality.
objectives: Read a COSC or similar certificate as a protocol, not a personality
Predict what a certificate does not say about magnetism or a worn jewel

concepts.name: Silicon hairsprings and escapes
concepts.summary: A material that does not magnetize and does not rust.
objectives: Use silicon for temperature, magnetism, and lubrication reasons you can name
Contrast a silicon hairspring with a steel one on those three axes
